paragraphs.text: 1. IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour.
paragraphs.original: तदिदास भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं यतो जज्ञ उग्रस्त्वेषनृम्णः ।
paragraphs.translit: tadidāsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ yato jajña ugrastveṣanṛmṇaḥ |

paragraphs.text: As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.
paragraphs.original: सद्यो जज्ञानो नि रिणाति शत्रूननु यं विश्वे मदन्त्यूमाः
paragraphs.translit: sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūnanu yaṃ viśve madantyūmāḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dasa,
paragraphs.original: वावृधानः शवसा भूर्योजाः शत्रुर्दासाय भियसं दधाति ।
paragraphs.translit: vāvṛdhānaḥ śavasā bhūryojāḥ śatrurdāsāya bhiyasaṃ dadhāti |

paragraphs.text: Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
paragraphs.original: अव्यनच्च व्यनच्च सस्नि सं ते नवन्त प्रभृता मदेषु
paragraphs.translit: avyanacca vyanacca sasni saṃ te navanta prabhṛtā madeṣu

paragraphs.text: 3. All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants.
paragraphs.original: त्वे क्रतुमपि वृञ्जन्ति विश्वे द्विर्यदेते त्रिर्भवन्त्यूमाः ।
paragraphs.translit: tve kratumapi vṛñjanti viśve dviryadete trirbhavantyūmāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle.
paragraphs.original: स्वादोः स्वादीयः स्वादुना सृजा समदः सु मधु मधुनाभि योधीः
paragraphs.translit: svādoḥ svādīyaḥ svādunā sṛjā samadaḥ su madhu madhunābhi yodhīḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful.
paragraphs.original: इति चिद्धि त्वा धना जयन्तं मदेमदे अनुमदन्ति विप्राः ।
paragraphs.translit: iti ciddhi tvā dhanā jayantaṃ mademade anumadanti viprāḥ |

paragraphs.text: With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yatudhanas harm thee.
paragraphs.original: ओजीयो धृष्णो स्थिरमा तनुष्व मा त्वा दभन्यातुधाना दुरेवाः
paragraphs.translit: ojīyo dhṛṣṇo sthiramā tanuṣva mā tvā dabhanyātudhānā durevāḥ

paragraphs.text: 5. Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat.
paragraphs.original: त्वया वयं शाशद्महे रणेषु प्रपश्यन्तो युधेन्यानि भूरि ।
paragraphs.translit: tvayā vayaṃ śāśadmahe raṇeṣu prapaśyanto yudhenyāni bhūri |

paragraphs.text: I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.
paragraphs.original: चोदयामि त आयुधा वचोभिः सं ते शिशामि ब्रह्मणा वयांसि
paragraphs.translit: codayāmi ta āyudhā vacobhiḥ saṃ te śiśāmi brahmaṇā vayāṃsi

paragraphs.text: 6. Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skillful, most energetic, Aptya of the Aptyas:
He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.
paragraphs.original: आ दर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून्प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि
paragraphs.translit: ā darṣate śavasā sapta dānūnpra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri

paragraphs.text: 7. Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower.
paragraphs.original: नि तद्दधिषेऽवरं परं च यस्मिन्नाविथावसा दुरोणे ।
paragraphs.translit: ni taddadhiṣe'varaṃ paraṃ ca yasminnāvithāvasā duroṇe |

paragraphs.text: Thou establishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.
paragraphs.original: आ मातरा स्थापयसे जिगत्नू अत इनोषि कर्वरा पुरूणि
paragraphs.translit: ā mātarā sthāpayase jigatnū ata inoṣi karvarā purūṇi

paragraphs.text: 8. Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra.
paragraphs.original: इमा ब्रह्म बृहद्दिवो विवक्तीन्द्राय शूषमग्रियः स्वर्षाः ।
paragraphs.translit: imā brahma bṛhaddivo vivaktīndrāya śūṣamagriyaḥ svarṣāḥ |

paragraphs.text: He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.
paragraphs.original: महो गोत्रस्य क्षयति स्वराजो दुरश्च विश्वा अवृणोदप स्वाः
paragraphs.translit: maho gotrasya kṣayati svarājo duraśca viśvā avṛṇodapa svāḥ

paragraphs.text: 9. Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person.
The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.
paragraphs.original: स्वसारो मातरिभ्वरीररिप्रा हिन्वन्ति च शवसा वर्धयन्ति च
paragraphs.translit: svasāro mātaribhvarīrariprā hinvanti ca śavasā vardhayanti ca
